subject: Throughput guarantee playbook and measurement matrix
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@aurelia.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput guarantee playbook and measurement matrix

Hi Maria —

Great to meet last week. Per our call, I’m attaching a concise playbook that describes how Redwood validates Dedicated throughput guarantees (tokens/sec and requests/sec) and the associated latency targets. High level: we tie guaranteed throughput to a reserved GPU commit, validate with a pre-cutover benchmark run, and include an ongoing measurement matrix that’s sampled at 1-minute resolution into the Console for visibility.

Key asks from your side: a representative traffic trace (or synthetic profile) and a target P99 latency SLO. We can run the pre-production verification inside your VPC or in a Redwood sandbox — whichever you prefer. I’ve attached a one-page matrix (RI-Dedicated-Throughput-Playbook-v1.pdf) and an anonymized CSV of a sample test run.

Summary of the proposed guarantee (draft):
- Committed pool: 8xA100 (or equivalent)
- Baseline throughput guarantee: 120k tokens/sec aggregate (sustained, 95% monthly availability)
- Request-level guardrail: 750 requests/sec concurrent with average 512-token context length
- Latency targets: median < 50ms token gen; P99 end-to-end < 350ms for streaming enabled calls (measured on the sample profile)

We recommend a two-week validation window before the contract effective date and a 30-day canary (live traffic at 10–20%). If verification shows a >10% delta vs the guaranteed numbers, we’ll propose either a capacity bump or a pro-rated credit depending on root cause.

Next steps: can you share a 48–72 hour traffic extract (or confirm we should synthesize with the attached sample), and confirm whether procurement wants the throughput guarantee expressed as tokens/sec or as requests/sec tiers?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the matrix.

—Jonas

jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Maria Gomez <maria@aurelia.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee playbook and measurement matrix

Jonas —

Thanks for the doc and the quick summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we circulate this to Procurement/CTO: 
1) How do you measure 'aggregate tokens/sec' when we run multi-tenant flows across multiple model variants? Will Redwood normalize across model family (e.g., Llama2-70B vs. 13B) or do we need separate guarantees per model?
2) P99: is the measurement service-side only, or end-to-end from our app through to the response? We need to understand whether client-side network variance is excluded.
3) Credits: can you be explicit about the crediting formula? We have internal procurement rules that require a deterministic calculation rather than a case-by-case ops review.

Also, procurement will ask whether the guarantee can be expressed as 'requests/sec with max tokens per request' since our traffic is spiky and more request-oriented. Could you provide a short table that maps tokens/sec <> requests/sec at a few token-per-request tiers?

cc: Evan (CTO) and procurement.

—Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurelia Systems
maria@aurelia.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@aurelia.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee playbook and measurement matrix

Maria —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions. I’ll address each and add concrete numbers so procurement has a deterministic formula they can bake into the contract.

1) Model normalization: we express the guarantee in two convertible ways — tokens/sec (aggregate compute-normalized) and requests/sec (by capped token-per-request tiers). In practice Redwood defines a 'compute unit' per model family based on measured token throughput on a standard hardware profile. For the Aurelia profile we propose using the 13B-equivalent baseline to avoid over-crediting. 

2) Measurement boundary: guaranteed latency and throughput are measured server-side inside the Redwood Dedicated runtime (post-ingress, pre-egress), with optional synthetic active probes run from within the customer's VPC for end-to-end checks. Contract language will exclude internet transit variability; we report both server-side and end-to-end as separate metrics.

3) Credit formula (deterministic):
- If observed monthly sustained throughput (server-side aggregate) < guaranteed throughput by X% for the billing month, credit = monthly commit fee * min(1.0, X / GuaranteedTolerance) * SLACoefficient.
- GuaranteedTolerance = 5% (buffer before credits apply). SLACoefficient = 0.6 for throughput incidents.

Example: guaranteed 120k tokens/sec, observed sustained 100k tokens/sec => X = 16.7% -> credit = commit_fee * min(1, 16.7/5) * 0.6 = commit_fee * 1 * 0.6 = 0.6 * commit_fee (pro-rated for incident duration).

Mapping table (excerpt):
- 256 tokens/request -> 468 requests/sec ≈ 120k tokens/sec
- 512 tokens/request -> 234 requests/sec ≈ 120k tokens/sec
- 128 tokens/request -> 937 requests/sec ≈ 120k tokens/sec

We can produce a full matrix that includes different model families and sequence length distributions; I’ll attach that as a CSV. For contract simplicity, many customers pick two tiers (steady-state and burst) and we express guarantees separately for each.

Operational notes: pre-cutover verification is a 72-hour run that must cover your 95th-percentile sequence-length distribution. The 30-day canary is used to validate the production routing and autoscale behaviors; credits only apply after the contract effective date.

Would you like us to translate the deterministic formula into procurement-friendly contract language (we can provide a short clause and a runnable metric query)?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

[Attachment: throughput-measurement-matrix-Aurelia.csv]

From: Maria Gomez <maria@aurelia.ai>

Cc: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@aurelia.ai>, procurement@aurelia.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee playbook and measurement matrix

Karthik —

This is exactly the level of specificity we needed, thank you. Procurement is comfortable with the deterministic credit formula and the two-tier mapping table; CTO wants the guarantee expressed as requests/sec at two token caps (256 and 512) for contract clarity, with a side table that converts to tokens/sec for billing reconciliation.

Two small asks before we proceed to signature: 
1) Can Redwood run the 72-hour validation inside our VPC (preferred) and provide the raw metric stream so our SREs can independently verify the server-side numbers? If yes, include the expected AWS IAM role and minimal firewall rules required.
2) Can we get the proposed contract clause text (two paragraphs) that implements the credit formula you shared? Procurement wants the exact wording.

If you can get those two items to us by EOD Monday Nov 15 we’ll aim to have Legal/Procurement review the contract the following week.

—Maria
